title: MLB proposes transaction reforms to reduce roster churn in CBA talks
dek: MLB presented proposals to the Players Association focused on reducing roster churn through transaction reforms, including a restricted free-agency window and month-long transaction freeze. The proposals center on restoring traditional full-time player roles and fan engagement.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: MLB presented transaction-focused proposals to the MLBPA as part of ongoing CBA negotiations.
bottom_line: MLB's emphasis on transaction reforms signals management's negotiating priorities for the next collective bargaining agreement. Watch for the union's formal response and any movement toward compromise on the specific terms of roster stability measures.
body: MLB presented proposals to the Players Association on Thursday as part of ongoing collective bargaining agreement negotiations, according to MLB.com.

Thursday's proposals centered on transactions, with the stated goal of reducing roster churn, restoring traditional full-time Major League roles for players, and creating more fan engagement during both the regular season and playoffs, per the report.

The source material provided does not include specific details on the proposed restricted free-agency window parameters, the month-long transaction freeze mechanics, or other transaction reforms. No MLBPA response or counterproposal is available in the sourced material, nor is a timeline for negotiations or a CBA deadline specified.
